title: Analytical and Asymptotic Modeling of Coupled Transient Gas Redistribution Induced by Simultaneous Injection and Withdrawal in Transmission Pipelines
content: This study develops an analytical and computational framework for investigating coupled transient gas redistribution induced by simultaneous localized injection and withdrawal in transmission pipelines. Unlike conventional transient-flow approaches that treat inflow and outflow processes independently, the proposed formulation establishes a unified coupled source-sink model capable of describing their dynamic interaction within a single transmission system. Using the Charny regularization approach, the governing equations of one-dimensional non-stationary isothermal compressible gas flow are transformed into a diffusion-type formulation. The pipeline is decomposed into three interacting spatial regions connected through continuity-based pressure and mass-flux interface conditions, and closed-form analytical solutions for the dimensionless pressure field are derived in the Laplace domain. A practical Laplace-domain approximation is introduced for computational evaluation of transient pressure redistribution. The results reveal the existence of a characteristic balancing point separating injection-dominated and withdrawal-dominated behavior and demonstrate rapid convergence toward a quasi-steady redistribution regime. Optimization analysis shows that redistribution-induced hydraulic disturbance is minimized near a balanced source-sink operating condition. The proposed framework provides new mathematical and physical insight into coupled transient redistribution phenomena and extends the analytical theory of non-stationary gas dynamics through coupled redistribution analysis, asymptotic stabilization behavior, and redistribution-oriented optimization within a unified Laplace-domain formulation.
